messages:
maria: quick sync — I'm drafting admission criteria for a low-latency L10n lane (focus: ja/ko/ar). we need a bench spec + a version-freeze TTL for customers who require deterministic responses. initial ideas?
aj: +1. propose two SLA lanes: 'interactive' (p95 < 150ms) and 'background' (p95 < 400ms). for L10n add tokenization/regression checks and a character-coverage report.
devin: agree on lanes. add cold-start budget target: <=20ms warm-up overhead ideally. also need an automatic fallback rule: if p95 breaches for 3 consecutive 5m windows, route to compatible smaller-family variant.
sarah: a customer asked whether we can avoid surprise swaps mid-contract — what do folks think about a freeze window and exception process?
maria: thinking of default version-freeze = 90d for self-serve, 180d for enterprise add-on. emergency rollouts (security/major bug) can override with 7d notice + automatic canary. exceptions tracked in ticketing.
aj: ops note: physical capacity may still force changes. we should define graceful-degrade ordering: same-family distillation -> lower-precision quant -> compatible-arch fallback. prefer to avoid cross-architecture swaps during business hours.
devin: here's a starter bench command we can standardize across eng/research:
```bash
# run lang-slab microbench for admission tests
./bench --model $MODEL --lang ja --seq 1024 --p95 --cold-start --concurrency 1 --samples 500
```
Key outputs we rely on: p50, p95, cold-start-ms, tokens/sec, decode-cost, tokenization-delta.
sarah: acceptance quality gates: for translation-style tasks require embedding-similarity >= 0.92 on k=1k pairs or chrF >= 0.48. for generation/assistant flows require no regression on curated prompts (diff < 1% hallucination rate).
maria: add rollout controls: canary at 1% tenant traffic for 24h, 5% for 24h, then ramp. rollback triggers: latency p95 regression > 15% or quality-signal drop > 2% on eval set.
aj: we also need a customer-visible SLA doc snippet: what they can expect when freeze is active, and our notice windows for emergency changes. ops needs that for sales.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for ja-l10n-slab run_id=20261107-42, started_by=maria, targets=canary-tier.
devin: one more ask — for long-tail languages capture tokenization edge-cases (emoji, mixed-script). add a small adversarial suite to the bench.
maria: sounds good. I'll spin up a PR that contains: bench script, acceptance thresholds, freeze TTLs, rollback triggers, and comm text for customers. tagging @aj @devin @sarah for review. will aim to get the PR up by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
